Chord Entry

Play the chords of a tune on a MIDI keyboard (or click them on the keys below) and they are written out as a chart. Check it, then send it to the Backing Track page, where the band plays it. With the chords in, you can also play the melody along with the band and have it written as notes. How it decides what to write, and a bench to see it at work on your last take.

1. Set up

Tonality

ms

ms

How the notes are written

3. Check

Words

How the line under the notes works

A draft puts one syllable on each note: the second half of a tied note is skipped (*), rests take nothing. Where a syllable is held over several notes add _ for each extra note; where a note has no word put *. A draft follows the words and the melody as they change; once you edit a line it is yours and is left alone.

The song file (ChordPro)

The song as a ChordPro file, with each section's melody and the words under it written in: what Download .cho saves. Change it here (chords, grids, sections, words, the ABC) and press "Use this text": the page reads the whole song again from it. Voicings and the undo history do not survive that.

4. Send it on

The ABC holds the chords, key, meter and title. The style, the tempo and any voicings you played in are not part of ABC: they travel only with "Open in the Backing Track".
